assumptions.summary: Drone flight height is capped at 4,000 m based on common market parameters.
Several mobile EOCs may be dispatched and provide charging and whole-process drone control.
Southeast wind is treated as representative during Victoria's summer-autumn fire season.
Orbost measurements are treated as representative of the entire selected fire area.
SSA observation range is treated as equivalent to the movement range of front-line personnel.
One or two peaks per 20 km justify a single-peak rather than multi-obstacle propagation model.
A 4 km operating altitude and the paper's signal threshold are used to infer 18-18.5 km terrain ranges.
Three SSA shifts are assumed sufficient for uninterrupted front-line coverage.
Repeater distance alone is used to choose two or three airframes for a relay role.
Southeast wind motivates a 45-degree projected fire-length direction.
A single long temperature series is treated as sufficient for decade fire planning.
Extreme fire is approximated by uniform expansion of the January 4 source field.
Mobile EOCs are required to be near high mountains so repeaters can be placed away from blocking terrain.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Fire records cover Australia in 2019-2020; January 4, 2020 is selected as the largest active-fire coverage day from October 2019 through July 2020.
Eastern Victoria fire records are planarized and meshed, with one-kilometre elevation sampling.
Grid severity combines fire frequency, satellite temperature, and satellite brightness.
Fire cells are joined to corresponding elevation values before placement and propagation calculations.
The DEM observation that only one or two peaks occur per 20 km configures the diffraction simplification.
A literature radio-loss relation and a 4 km flight altitude configure the 18-18.5 km range estimate.
Endurance is stated as 2.5 hours, charging as 1.75 hours, and maximum SSA-EOC distance as 30 km.
A 10,000 AUD unit price is applied to both SSA and repeater airframes.
Daily maximum and minimum temperature from 1938-2020 are preprocessed with linear interpolation.
Dated MODIS fire-site counts from August 2019-January 2020 are aligned with temperature and normalized.
The maximum forecast fire-site count 2698.14 is converted to an 8.84 percent increase over the source maximum.
The January 4 boundary is expanded uniformly by factor 1.0884 to form the extreme map.
Problem 3 uses accumulated fire coverage from October 1, 2019 through January 7, 2020 and the corresponding DEM.
Sixteen final latitude-longitude pairs are tabulated for repeater placement.
Seven references provide partial context, equipment, fire-data, weather, propagation, and mapping provenance.

Score each fire grid from frequency and a convex combination of satellite temperature and brightness.
Relate frequency and path distance to baseline propagation loss before terrain diffraction.

Align dated fire-site counts with temperature and fit an exponential relation used to select the maximum future fire-site count.
Expand the January 4 fire field by 1.0884 to simulate an extreme next-decade condition.
Rerun the base model on the expanded map and report changes in repeater, SSA, and equipment cost.
Extend the base repeater search to accumulated fires and terrain-specific obstruction zones.
Require mobile EOCs to lie within 20 distance units of a high mountain before repeater placement.
Restrict repeater communication range using mountain distance and relative height before the final genetic search.
Use the EOC and terrain-range constraints to report nine EOCs and sixteen repeater latitude-longitude pairs.
Vary drone flight altitude around 4 km and inspect the resulting repeater signal range.

results_trace.summary: At 4 km flight altitude, the peak-limited communication range is reported as approximately 18.5 km and complex-terrain range as approximately 18 km.
The exchange-period argument claims three SSA shifts can cover front-line personnel continuously.
The base genetic search reports 24 radio-repeater airframes.
Projected fire-length sizing reports 30 SSA airframes.
The base budget is 24 x 10,000 plus 30 x 10,000 = 540,000 AUD.
The maximum next-decade fire-site estimate is 2698.14, reported as 8.84 percent above the source maximum.
The extreme spatial field is created by multiplying source fire area by 1.0884.
Extreme rerun: EOCs unchanged, repeaters increase 24 to 27, and SSA airframes increase 30 to 48.
The extreme fleet totals 750,000 AUD, an arithmetically correct 210,000 AUD increase despite a component typo.
The terrain-aware EOC genetic search is described as finding nine mobile EOCs.
The terrain-aware repeater search reports sixteen latitude-longitude pairs.
A plus/minus 5 percent altitude change is interpreted as roughly plus 1.67/minus 2.78 percent signal-range change.
The Budget Request asks CFA to fund the base 30-SSA/24-repeater fleet before the next fire season.

weaknesses.summary: The fire score gives no fitted or elicited values for k_1 and k_2, no scale reconciliation, and no validation that the weighted score measures operational severity.
The printed five-piece diffraction-loss relation has overlapping intervals and incomplete semantics; it is preserved rather than silently repaired.
The stated average altitude of 551.8 km is almost certainly a metre/kilometre unit error and cannot be used literally.
The three-airframe claim lacks a complete endurance, travel, charging, overlap, reserve, failure, and launch timeline.
The two repeater-count branches both include d_m = 13.5 km, so the equality case is contradictory.
The EOC and repeater genetic algorithms omit population size, encoding bounds, crossover and mutation rates, stopping rule, seeds, and repeated-run stability.
The 24-repeater, 30-SSA result lacks frozen inputs, candidate sets, solver traces, intermediate coverage states, and an exact or heuristic baseline.
The LSTM supplies no architecture, hyperparameters, train/validation split, baseline comparison, seed, residual diagnostics, uncertainty, or code.
The regression uses only 2019-2020 fire observations, omits holdout scoring and uncertainty, and does not control for fuel, wind, rainfall, ignition, suppression, or spatial dependence.
Uniform 1.0884 spatial expansion preserves source shape and ignores spread direction, fuel, weather, barriers, suppression, ignition, and correlated uncertainty.
The printed SSA cost increase of 18,000 AUD conflicts with 18 additional drones at 10,000 AUD each; 180,000 AUD is required for the stated 210,000 AUD total increase.
The EOC-near-high-mountain rationale is unclear, and the terrain-dependent repeater-range relation has an ambiguous piecewise layout and incomplete units.
The sixteen repeater coordinates form an unusually regular sequence and are not supported by candidate data, objective values, feasibility traces, or independent radio measurements.
Sensitivity varies only flight altitude from 3.6 to 4.4 km and does not test model structure, fire inputs, weights, GA randomness, schedules, costs, interactions, or decision-rank stability.
The budget prices only the two drone categories and gives little item-level quotation, lifecycle, staffing, battery, maintenance, training, tax, contingency, or uncertainty justification.
The body reaches Page 21 of 20, and physical pages 24-25 carry Team 2120188 in the header while the paper and signature identify Team 2127300.
